title: AOV-GS: Active Open-Vocabulary Semantic Mapping with 3D Gaussian Splatting
venue: AIST 2026, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 16795, pp. 312-328, Springer, Cham (2027)

problem.summary: Robots deployed in human-centered environments need maps that support both geometric navigation and open-vocabulary semantic queries beyond a fixed label set.
statements: Robots deployed in human-centered environments need maps that support both geometric navigation and open-vocabulary semantic queries beyond a fixed label set.
A key challenge is enriching such maps with semantic information without relying on manually annotated segmentation masks or closed-set semantic categories.

background.summary: Shkokov et al. during mapping determine geometric completeness, object visibility, and the evidence available for downstream open-vocabulary retrieval.

evidence.quote: Shkokov et al. during mapping determine geometric completeness, object visibility, and the evidence available for downstream open-vocabulary retrieval.
No established passive semantic baseline exists for this protocol; therefore, passive comparisons are reported only on Replica.

solution.summary: Exploration routes on office0: AOV-GS covers the central workspace more thoroughly than the geometry-only planner.
solution.approach: Exploration routes on office0: AOV-GS covers the central workspace more thoroughly than the geometry-only planner.
components: Semantic exploration is most beneficial when semantically distinctive objects occupy the central workspace and remain visible from multiple viewpoints.

On office0, the geometry-only planner favours peripheral unseen regions over the furniture-dense core (Fig. 6), yielding +7.1 pp mIoU over the geometry-only baseline (Table 1) and strong sofa/table coverage for AOV-GS (87.3%/84.3%).
Similar behaviour appears on office3 and office4 (+4.4 and +3.0 pp with CorrCLIP).

experiments.summary: Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) SLAM systems [13, 11] achieve efficient high-fidelity reconstruction suitable for online robotic mapping.

evidence.quote: Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) SLAM systems [13, 11] achieve efficient high-fidelity reconstruction suitable for online robotic mapping.
Active planners such as ActiveGS [10], ActiveSplat [19], and ActiveGAMER [3] improve coverage through geometry-aware next-best-view (NBV) selection.

limitations.summary: Across Replica and Matterport3D, the resulting maps improve average open-vocabulary language-field mIoU over geometry-only exploration while preserving comparable novel-view reconstruction quality.
items: Across Replica and Matterport3D, the resulting maps improve average open-vocabulary language-field mIoU over geometry-only exploration while preserving comparable novel-view reconstruction quality.
Replica gains vary by scene, while the five-seed office0 experiment shows a consistent advantage over geometry-only exploration.

evidence.quote: Across Replica and Matterport3D, the resulting maps improve average open-vocabulary language-field mIoU over geometry-only exploration while preserving comparable novel-view reconstruction quality.
Replica gains vary by scene, while the five-seed office0 experiment shows a consistent advantage over geometry-only exploration.
ActiveSGM [4] demonstrates that semantic signals can guide exploration in a 3DGS loop, but relies on per-scene OneFormer [7] fine-tuning, which limits open-vocabulary deployment.
